title: Stop losing customer webhooks when their endpoint is down
summary:
A customer's endpoint was allowed to decide our request latency, and a failed delivery existed only as a line in a log. This change records every webhook before the request returns, sends it from a queue worker, retries only failures that can succeed later, and gives support a way to inspect and replay a delivery.

```text
pay order ──► record delivery ──► return
                    │
                    ▼
              queue worker ──► customer endpoint
                    │                 │
                    │      retryable? │
                    ▼                 ▼
               next attempt       delivered
```

The API call site keeps its shape: `dispatchWebhook` still takes an account and an event. What moved is the waiting, and with it the failure handling.

sections.title: The request path should not wait for a customer's server

steps.text:
`markOrderPaid` used to sign the payload and call the customer's endpoint inline. That tied our latency and success to a third party, and a crash after the order was written would drop the event with nothing recorded.

The call site keeps the same shape. `dispatchWebhook` now records the delivery and returns; signing moves to the sender, which is the only place that knows it is about to make a network call.

sections.title: Record a delivery before anything can fail

steps.text:
A delivery is a row, not a log line. `status` follows its journey, `attempts` is incremented when a worker claims it, and `next_attempt_at` is the only clock the queue reads.

The unique index on `(account_id, event_id)` makes recording idempotent: if the same API request is retried, the second insert is ignored instead of sending the customer a duplicate.
steps.diff:
diff --git a/db/migrations/0042_webhook_deliveries.sql b/db/migrations/0042_webhook_deliveries.sql
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/db/migrations/0042_webhook_deliveries.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+create table webhook_deliveries (
+  id text primary key,
+  account_id text not null,
+  event_id text not null,
+  event_type text not null,
+  payload jsonb not null,
+  endpoint text not null,
+  status text not null default 'queued'
+    check (status in ('queued', 'sending', 'delivered', 'exhausted')),
+  attempts integer not null default 0,
+  next_attempt_at timestamptz not null default now(),
+  last_error text,
+  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
+  delivered_at timestamptz
+);
+
+create unique index webhook_deliveries_account_event
+  on webhook_deliveries (account_id, event_id);
+
+create index webhook_deliveries_due
+  on webhook_deliveries (next_attempt_at)
+  where status = 'queued';

steps.text:
`enqueueDelivery` writes the event and its endpoint in one statement. The payload stays JSON so a later attempt sends exactly what was accepted, even if the order changes in the meantime.

`claimDueDeliveries` is the queue's handshake. It selects due rows, marks them `sending`, and increments `attempts` in one statement; `for update skip locked` lets several workers run without handing the same row to two of them.

The remaining functions close the loop after an attempt: delivered, queued again with the next time, or exhausted with the last error.
steps.diff:
diff --git a/src/webhooks/store.ts b/src/webhooks/store.ts
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/webhooks/store.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+import { query } from '../db'
+import type { WebhookEvent } from './dispatch'
+
+export interface QueuedDelivery {
+  id: string
+  accountId: string
+  eventId: string
+  eventType: string
+  payload: WebhookEvent
+  endpoint: string
+  attempts: number
+}
+
+export interface DeliveryRow {
+  id: string
+  account_id: string
+  event_id: string
+  event_type: string
+  payload: WebhookEvent
+  endpoint: string
+  attempts: number
+}
+
+export async function enqueueDelivery(
+  accountId: string,
+  event: WebhookEvent,
+  endpoint: string,
+): Promise<void> {
+  // The event ID is part of the identity: if a caller retries the API request, the
+  // delivery is already recorded and the second insert changes nothing.
+  await query(
+    `insert into webhook_deliveries (id, account_id, event_id, event_type, payload, endpoint)
+     values ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)
+     on conflict (account_id, event_id) do nothing`,
+    [`dlv_${crypto.randomUUID()}`, accountId, event.id, event.type, event, endpoint],
+  )
+}
+
+export async function claimDueDeliveries(limit: number): Promise<QueuedDelivery[]> {
+  // Claiming moves the row out of `queued` before any network call, so two workers
+  // cannot send the same attempt. A crash after this point leaves the row in
+  // `sending`; the next deploy can requeue stale rows.
+  const rows = await query<DeliveryRow>(
+    `update webhook_deliveries
+        set status = 'sending', attempts = attempts + 1
+      where id in (
+        select id
+          from webhook_deliveries
+         where status = 'queued' and next_attempt_at <= now()
+         order by next_attempt_at
+         limit $1
+         for update skip locked
+      )
+      returning id, account_id, event_id, event_type, payload, endpoint, attempts`,
+    [limit],
+  )
+  return rows.map(toDelivery)
+}
+
+export async function markDelivered(id: string): Promise<void> {
+  await query(
+    `update webhook_deliveries
+        set status = 'delivered', delivered_at = now(), last_error = null
+      where id = $1`,
+    [id],
+  )
+}
+
+export async function scheduleRetry(
+  id: string,
+  nextAttemptAt: Date,
+  error: string,
+): Promise<void> {
+  await query(
+    `update webhook_deliveries
+        set status = 'queued', next_attempt_at = $2, last_error = $3
+      where id = $1`,
+    [id, nextAttemptAt, error],
+  )
+}
+
+export async function markExhausted(id: string, error: string): Promise<void> {
+  await query(
+    `update webhook_deliveries
+        set status = 'exhausted', last_error = $2
+      where id = $1`,
+    [id, error],
+  )
+}
+
+export function toDelivery(row: DeliveryRow): QueuedDelivery {
+  return {
+    id: row.id,
+    accountId: row.account_id,
+    eventId: row.event_id,
+    eventType: row.event_type,
+    payload: row.payload,
+    endpoint: row.endpoint,
+    attempts: row.attempts,
+  }
+}

sections.title: Retry only what is worth retrying

steps.text:
`deliverOnce` sends one attempt and classifies the result. A 429 or a 5xx response means the endpoint is reachable but busy, so another try can succeed. A 4xx is a rejected payload or a missing route; repeating it would only repeat the same answer.

The ten second timeout keeps a silent endpoint from holding a worker slot indefinitely, and a thrown network error is treated as retryable.

The schedule is short and finite: 30 seconds, then 2, 10, 60, and 360 minutes. After the fifth attempt `retryAt` returns `null`, so the delivery becomes `exhausted` instead of retrying forever.

Five attempts is a product decision, not a technical limit. Keeping the delays in one array makes the policy easy to read and easy to change.
steps.diff:
diff --git a/src/webhooks/retry.ts b/src/webhooks/retry.ts
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/webhooks/retry.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+// Five attempts spread over roughly seven hours: long enough to ride out a customer's
+// deployment, short enough that support can still reason about when an event was last
+// sent. The last entry is the wait before the final attempt.
+const backoffSeconds = [30, 120, 600, 3600, 21_600]
+
+export const maxAttempts = backoffSeconds.length
+
+export function retryAt(attempt: number, now = Date.now()): Date | null {
+  const delay = backoffSeconds[attempt - 1]
+  return delay === undefined ? null : new Date(now + delay * 1000)
+}

sections.title: Let the queue own the waiting

steps.text:
`drainWebhookQueue` is the only place that decides what happens after an attempt. Each claimed delivery is resolved on its own, so one failing endpoint does not stop the batch.

The branch order matters: a missing endpoint is exhausted immediately, a permanent failure is not retried, and only a retryable failure consults `retryAt`. A crash after claiming leaves the row in `sending`, which is visible instead of silently lost.
steps.diff:
diff --git a/src/queue/webhooks.ts b/src/queue/webhooks.ts
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/queue/webhooks.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+import { recordDelivery } from '../observability/metrics'
+import { deliverOnce } from '../webhooks/deliver'
+import { endpointFor } from '../webhooks/endpoints'
+import { retryAt } from '../webhooks/retry'
+import {
+  claimDueDeliveries,
+  markDelivered,
+  markExhausted,
+  scheduleRetry,
+} from '../webhooks/store'
+
+export async function drainWebhookQueue(limit = 50): Promise<number> {
+  const deliveries = await claimDueDeliveries(limit)
+
+  for (const delivery of deliveries) {
+    const endpoint = endpointFor(delivery.accountId)
+    if (endpoint === null) {
+      await markExhausted(delivery.id, 'No endpoint is registered for this account')
+      recordDelivery('exhausted')
+      continue
+    }
+
+    const outcome = await deliverOnce(delivery, endpoint.secret)
+
+    if (outcome.kind === 'delivered') {
+      await markDelivered(delivery.id)
+      recordDelivery('delivered')
+      continue
+    }
+
+    if (outcome.kind === 'permanent-failure') {
+      await markExhausted(delivery.id, outcome.error)
+      recordDelivery('exhausted')
+      continue
+    }
+
+    const nextAttemptAt = retryAt(delivery.attempts)
+    if (nextAttemptAt === null) {
+      await markExhausted(delivery.id, outcome.error)
+      recordDelivery('exhausted')
+    } else {
+      await scheduleRetry(delivery.id, nextAttemptAt, outcome.error)
+      recordDelivery('retrying')
+    }
+  }
+
+  return deliveries.length
+}

steps.text: Counting the three outcomes separately makes the queue's health visible. A climbing `retrying` count means a customer is struggling; a climbing `exhausted` count means someone needs to act. The counters are process-local for now; the shape is what matters.

sections.title: Give support a way to look and replay

steps.text:
Two reads make the ledger useful. `deliveriesForAccount` lists recent attempts for one account, newest first, without exposing other customers' rows.

`requeueDelivery` deliberately revives only an `exhausted` row. Replaying a queued or already delivered delivery would send a duplicate, so requiring exhaustion keeps the operation safe to press.
steps.diff:
diff --git a/src/webhooks/history.ts b/src/webhooks/history.ts
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/webhooks/history.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+import { query } from '../db'
+import { toDelivery, type DeliveryRow, type QueuedDelivery } from './store'
+
+export async function deliveriesForAccount(
+  accountId: string,
+  limit = 50,
+): Promise<QueuedDelivery[]> {
+  const rows = await query<DeliveryRow>(
+    `select id, account_id, event_id, event_type, payload, endpoint, attempts
+       from webhook_deliveries
+      where account_id = $1
+      order by created_at desc
+      limit $2`,
+    [accountId, limit],
+  )
+  return rows.map(toDelivery)
+}
+
+// Replay only touches an exhausted delivery; a queued or delivered one already has
+// an owner and replaying it would send the customer a duplicate.
+export async function requeueDelivery(accountId: string, id: string): Promise<boolean> {
+  const rows = await query<{ id: string }>(
+    `update webhook_deliveries
+        set status = 'queued', attempts = 0, next_attempt_at = now(), last_error = null
+      where id = $1 and account_id = $2 and status = 'exhausted'
+      returning id`,
+    [id, accountId],
+  )
+  return rows.length > 0
+}

steps.text: The API layer stays thin: it names the two operations support needs and leaves the ownership rules to the store. `replayDelivery` answers whether anything changed, which the route turns into a status code.
steps.diff:
diff --git a/src/api/webhooks.ts b/src/api/webhooks.ts
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/api/webhooks.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+import { deliveriesForAccount, requeueDelivery, type QueuedDelivery } from '../webhooks/history'
+
+export async function listDeliveries(accountId: string): Promise<QueuedDelivery[]> {
+  return deliveriesForAccount(accountId)
+}
+
+export async function replayDelivery(accountId: string, deliveryId: string): Promise<boolean> {
+  return requeueDelivery(accountId, deliveryId)
+}

steps.text:
The admin routes read the account from a header, list deliveries, and replay one by ID. The route table is still a plain array; the new endpoints did not need a framework change.

`deliveryIdFrom` reads the same `:id` position the route declares, so the replay handler does not need a new parameter convention.

sections.title: Pin the schedule with a test

steps.text:
The test fixes both halves of the contract: the wait after each attempt and the moment retries stop. It also stubs `fetch` to prove that a 503 asks for another attempt while a 400 gives up.

These tests need neither a database nor a network, so they run in milliseconds and stay honest about the policy.
steps.diff:
diff --git a/test/webhooks/retry.test.ts b/test/webhooks/retry.test.ts
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/webhooks/retry.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
+import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test'
+import { deliverOnce } from '../../src/webhooks/deliver'
+import { maxAttempts, retryAt } from '../../src/webhooks/retry'
+import type { QueuedDelivery } from '../../src/webhooks/store'
+
+function delivery(): QueuedDelivery {
+  return {
+    id: 'dlv_1',
+    accountId: 'acct_1',
+    eventId: 'evt_1',
+    eventType: 'order.paid',
+    payload: {
+      id: 'evt_1',
+      type: 'order.paid',
+      data: { orderId: 'ord_1' },
+      createdAt: '2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z',
+    },
+    endpoint: 'https://customer.example/webhooks',
+    attempts: 1,
+  }
+}
+
+describe('retryAt', () => {
+  test('waits longer after each failed attempt', () => {
+    const now = Date.parse('2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z')
+
+    expect(retryAt(1, now)?.toISOString()).toBe('2026-10-01T00:00:30.000Z')
+    expect(retryAt(2, now)?.toISOString()).toBe('2026-10-01T00:02:00.000Z')
+    expect(retryAt(3, now)?.toISOString()).toBe('2026-10-01T00:10:00.000Z')
+  })
+
+  test('stops after the last attempt', () => {
+    expect(maxAttempts).toBe(5)
+    expect(retryAt(maxAttempts)).toBeNull()
+  })
+})
+
+describe('deliverOnce', () => {
+  test('keeps a 500 for another attempt and gives up on a 400', async () => {
+    const originalFetch = globalThis.fetch
+    try {
+      globalThis.fetch = (async () => new Response(null, { status: 503 })) as typeof fetch
+      expect(await deliverOnce(delivery(), 'secret')).toEqual({
+        kind: 'retry',
+        error: 'HTTP 503',
+      })
+
+      globalThis.fetch = (async () => new Response(null, { status: 400 })) as typeof fetch
+      expect(await deliverOnce(delivery(), 'secret')).toEqual({
+        kind: 'permanent-failure',
+        error: 'HTTP 400',
+      })
+    } finally {
+      globalThis.fetch = originalFetch
+    }
+  })
+})
